company: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd
basis: Consolidated, Rs Crore unless noted. Source: https://www.screener.in/company/CGPOWER/consolidated/, fetched 2026-09-24. Only FY2015-FY2019 pulled (5yr window bracketing the single FY2016 scoring date rather than 5yr trailing) -- see data_quality_flags.
capex_proxy_caveat: Same caveat as other names: 'capex_proxy_cr' = 'Cash from Investing Activity' total.
net_debt_proxy_caveat: Gross Borrowings used as net-debt proxy; cash/bank balances not broken out at this fetch depth.
restatement_warning: FY2018 (and possibly FY2019) figures shown below are Screener's CURRENT (post-2019-fraud-investigation, restated) values, not as originally filed -- see sourced_eps/cgpower.json for the original-vs-restated deltas found for FY2018. FY2016 (the scored year) was not confirmed restated but also not confirmed clean beyond the absence of a specific restatement report found in the sources searched.

FY2016.note: The only scored CG Power date. Revenue DOWN 9% YoY, EBITDA margin collapsed from 5.0% to 1.7%, net loss Rs -461cr (EPS -7.33) despite this margin drop being relatively mild -- the loss is driven mainly by Other Income turning sharply negative (-Rs230cr, likely a one-off/exceptional charge) plus continued high interest cost on Rs 1,528cr of borrowings.

FY2017.note: Operating profit turns negative outright; Working Capital Days spikes from 47 to 283 -- a large, visible deterioration in working-capital efficiency the year immediately after the scored FY16 date.

FY2018.note: RESTATED figures (see restatement_warning). Revenue jump partly reflects business changes; borrowings continue climbing to Rs 3,041cr.

FY2019.note: FY in which the fraud was publicly disclosed (Aug 2019). Net loss -Rs1,331cr, by far the largest in the window -- this is the print investors actually saw the collapse in.

beta: 0.81 (current, 2026, per topstockresearch.com/tipranks-style aggregators) -- explicitly a PRESENT-DAY figure under the post-2020 Murugappa/Tube Investments ownership and much-changed capital structure, NOT usable as a point-in-time FY2016 input; provided only as supplementary context, not for use in a PIT DCF at the 2016-03-31 scoring date. No FY2016-era beta was located.
forensic_flags_visible_as_of_scoring_dat: As of 2016-03-31 (the ONLY scored date): the company was ALREADY loss-making (Net Profit -Rs461cr, FY16) with Debtor Days elevated at 144 (though actually down from a presumably higher pre-FY15 level -- FY15 was 194) and revenue declining -9% YoY. This is a company already showing real operating distress three-plus years before the fraud became public in Aug 2019 -- a diligent FY2016 analyst reading only the published numbers would have seen a leveraged, loss-making, shrinking industrial name, i.e. enough to flag it as a poor DCF candidate on fundamentals ALONE, without needing to anticipate the later-discovered fraud.

The specific accounting fraud (undisclosed liabilities, related-party fund diversion, overstated bank balances) was NOT disclosed until Aug 2019 and by its nature involved concealment -- so the FORENSIC-fraud element specifically was not PIT-detectable from the FY2016 numbers alone. What WAS detectable at FY2016 was plain operating deterioration (margin collapse, swing to loss, revenue decline), which is a distinct and much earlier signal than the fraud disclosure itself.

Working Capital Days trajectory (84 -> 47 -> 283 -> -53 -> -96, FY15-FY19) is erratic/non-monotonic in a way that is itself a mild data-quality flag -- large swings in either direction can reflect either genuine operational volatility or the restatements distorting the comparative base; not resolved further here.
